facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of a slowly growing, dull, intermittent swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule
fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area
teeth #15 and #16 were grossly carious
a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa
no tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth
a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices
a provisional diagnosis of a periapical abscess was made
preoperative blood tests were within normal limits
curettage yielded a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue
a provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma

The patient's symptoms and radiographic findings, including the mild periapical radiolucency, could also be consistent with a periapical cyst, which is a possible diagnosis given the presence of a grossly carious tooth and a firm, mildly tender swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa.

The patient's presentation of a slowly growing swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, along with the presence of grossly carious teeth and a mild periapical radiolucency, also supports the diagnosis of a periapical abscess, which was the initial provisional diagnosis made based on the clinical and radiographic findings.

The patient's symptoms and radiographic findings, including the mild periapical radiolucency, could also be consistent with chronic periapical periodontitis, which is a possible diagnosis given the presence of a grossly carious tooth and a firm, mildly tender swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa.

The patient's presentation of a slowly growing swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, along with the presence of grossly carious teeth and the curettage yielding a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue, supports the diagnosis of a dental granuloma, which is a possible diagnosis given the clinical and histopathological findings.
